review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner (self-review, not independent approval)
review.decision: Separate durable HQ replies from Codex queued human turns, and make recent chat reads explicit and recoverable
review.notes: User explicitly requested repair of overnight relay backlog and large-session chat loading. Keep original queues and original records intact. New Codex replies stay in a source-scoped durable inbox; at most one small notice per exact active turn, fresh replies only, no queued full bodies, no idle turn/start or queue fallback on unsupported/ambiguous outcomes. A notice acceptance is not a read; fetched means only the source CLI returned the reply, never proof a model acted. New source guidance uses inbox/wait at natural boundaries. Preserve legacy accepted delivery attribution and other agent dispatch behavior. Recent chat is an opt-in20-turn read; older API default and context/authorization remain. Mobile paging must preserve original identities, update latest data without dropping fetched older pages, reject stale cross-target results and leave content on transient failure. No live queue, restore, service, App, TCC or deployment operation. Existing valid tests remain unchanged; new files use controlled transport/ledger/RN fixtures. Static/isolated checks do not certify live Codex/frontend or device behavior. Refined before notice-attribution tests: a compact hint must still appear as HQ, established by exact durable accepted Notice receipt plus first eligible source record, not merely its textual marker. CLI fetched_at means the source command fetched saved data, not successful stdout/model reading. Mobile record_id takes precedence over index-based fallback for state/keys when prepending source pages. The original default API empty/error compatibility remains unchanged; new recent behavior is opt-in. Before authorization-loss regression implementation: transient page errors keep content, but401/403 must retire the loaded history for that exact recent snapshot immediately. A subsequent authoritative snapshot can recover; an old denial cannot hide a newer snapshot. This preserves the existing screen auth-retirement behavior with the new shared history prefix. Final paging refinement before the corresponding regression: an explicit earlier-HQ-session stitch can prepend a different source session while current-session pages are already loaded. Merge by source-session order and original ordinal with recent data winning same IDs; do not append a predecessor after the newest session. A fetched50-turn history page mounts at most the next20 turns initially; retained pages do not force all50 native rows at once. Preserve the reader anchor for both a source page and an in-memory window expansion. Cancellation cleanup refinement before test implementation: abort on unmount/identity change must reject the bounded race and clear its deadline even when a synthetic reader ignores AbortSignal. This is a test-only noncooperative reader; no claim a live network leak was observed. Before contention regression: bounded source wait must honor cancellation while the relay ledger lock is held. Use a real isolated flock and an observed lock-attempt barrier, not sleep-based ordering; keep the reply unconsumed. Context-aware notification claims/receipts share transport/short receipt budgets. This covers ordinary lock contention, not uninterruptible kernel I/O.

cases.description: Strict active-only HQ notice RPC never queues or starts turns
cases.setup: Synthetic initialized Codex peer with exact home/backend/thread, active/idle/unloaded/approval/unsupported/direct capability and receipt cases
cases.action: Call actual coordination input path; decode every wire request and final guard/turn ID
cases.expected: Only eligible active exact turn can receive one turn/steer. Idle/unloaded/unsupported/mismatched/blocked states cause zero mutating writes; even definitive unknown-method after steer has no queue fallback. Missing acceptance remains attempted/unknown. No thread catalog/resume, no turn/start or thread/queue/add. Required scope check runs before mutation; rejected check has no side effects. A negative control restoring old queued semantics fails wire assertions, not setup.

cases.description: Durable inbox owns receipt truth, freshness and per-turn burst coalescing
cases.setup: Isolated state directory with multiple requests across homes/threads and old accepted legacy entries
cases.action: Resolve replies, claim notice concurrently for same active turn, complete notification/fetch, list inbox, expire a reply, and re-open store
cases.expected: ReplyAt is set once, legacy entries unchanged/readable, never reset age on identical resolve. Only one notification claim per home/thread/active turn; unknown blocks another notice in that turn. Different turn or identity independent. Expired/legacy/already fetched replies do not auto notify; body stays durable. Source fetch is exact-identity checked and idempotent and does not set Delivered or claim model execution. Unfetched listing bounded and deterministic; no existing request deletion/replay. A source Wait cancelled after observing a real contended ledger lock returns without waiting for lock release and leaves fetched_at zero.

cases.description: Application uses inbox plus short active notice and source-owned pull/wait
cases.setup: Isolated real relay ledger with controlled native RPC seam; source identities exact and changed; no actual process/session input
cases.action: Call actual Codex relay delivery and source inbox/show/wait helpers against saved replies
cases.expected: Codex delivery never enters legacy tmux/queue fallback; notice text excludes complete reply/private body, accepted status describes notice only. Burst guard and freshness rechecked at mutation. CLI source pull fetches only own home/thread/pane lifetime; timeout/cancel bounded with reply left intact, no busy indefinite wait. Late reply returned through tool output on pull, not new human turn. Legacy delivered rows not replayed; original caller authorization retained. The canonical short inbox hint is attributed to HQ only with accepted exact-home/thread receipt and first source witness; a later human copy remains human.

cases.description: Recent transcript endpoint is opt-in and history does not require a heavy default load
cases.setup: Authorized isolated server/pane transcript dependencies with independent default/recent counters and history cursor hook
cases.action: Request recent=1/default/before/guest and compare ETAG scopes and original ordinals
cases.expected: Default stays compatible; recent request selects20-turn producer; before page invokes history after identity authorization using metadata-only producer without default full parse. ETag distinguishes recent/full; request scope and guest context stripping unchanged. History cursor reaches all earlier source turns with original numbering; unsupported recent dependency falls back safely. Invalid recent value rejected or treated as default, never guessed limits.

cases.description: Shared App chat fetches recent data and loads source history with honest failure UX
cases.setup: Controlled RN Detail/HQ/Chat fixtures with deferred transcript/history requests and original session/home/client identity
cases.action: Open chat, fail then retry, load earlier pages, poll latest, switch target while old page resolves
cases.expected: Initial requests opt into recent20, prior API call defaults preserved. Shared chat offers real load-earlier control for server-dropped records/cursor; already fetched earlier turns survive live polling; duplicate IDs not doubled; no stale result or content crosses target/client/home/session. Loading/error/retry is explicit; transient failures retain shown content and allow retry instead of blank or endless spinner. Source history error retains content/cursor. No caching credentials or unverified identities. Actual RN interaction assertions cover both screens and shared UI; no native/device performance claim. Prefer stable record_id for disclosure keys across prepends. Verify actual GtmuxClient recent query opt-in and default URL compatibility. History401/403 retires its exact displayed snapshot and prefix immediately; a fresh authoritative snapshot recovers, while a stale denial does not overwrite newer content. Existing current-session pages and explicit predecessor-session stitching stay chronological; source paging grows the mounted window by at most20, with anchor retained on both source and in-memory prepends. Unmount/identity abort releases the deadline timer without waiting for a noncooperative reader; no update reaches the disposed view.
